api.name: Regional Rail, LLC
api.description: Regional Rail owns and operates short-line freight railroads and related rail services across the United States and Canada. Its customer base spans industrial, agricultural, chemicals, aggregates, food, and logistics end markets that depend on local freight connectivity and transload services. The company follows an asset-heavy operating model built around owned and leased track, rail-served industrial infrastructure, and operating railroad franchises. Public disclosures describe a network of more than 875 route miles, 17 railroad operations, and approximately 65,000 annual carloads as of 2023. api.name: Chief Power
api.description: Chief Power is an ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V-backed merchant-generation platform holding partial tenant-in-common interests in the Keystone and Conemaugh coal-fired generating stations in western Pennsylvania. ArcLight established the platform in 2014 and expanded it through a separately financed acquisition in 2019. After a 2020 lender restructuring transferred control of the original tranche, Fund V retained a small minority voting interest and continued to control the separately owned Chief Power Finance II tranche. Current public filings identify Fund V as holding greater than 10% voting interests in each II plant-owner entity, while the exact Fund V economic percentage is not publicly disclosed. Chief Power is the single PortCo; its financing entities, transfer parent, plant-owner subsidiaries and the two jointly owned generating stations are not separate portfolio companies.

ArcLight's separately financed Chief II entities completed the acquisition of PSEG's 22.84% Keystone and 22.5% Conemaugh interests.
Chief Power acquired additional minority interests, increasing its original tranche to 44.45% of Keystone and 35.11% of Conemaugh.
ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V completed the acquisition of Exelon's 41.98% Keystone and 31.28% Conemaugh ownership interests and established the Chief Power platform.

api.name: Orca Acquisitions, LLC
api.subsector: Merchant power generation and industrial steam
api.description: Orca Acquisitions, LLC is an ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VI and Olympus Power joint-venture platform that indirectly owns Walleye Power, LLC through Walleye Energy Holdings, LLC. Walleye owns and operates the Bay Shore merchant-power and industrial-steam facility in Oregon, Ohio. A June 2026 FERC filing reports 136 MW of summer-rated steam generation and a 16 MW oil-fired unit. ArcLight Orca Holdings, LLC holds 95% of Orca's Class A managing interests, appoints two management-committee members and controls day-to-day decisions. Olympus affiliates hold the remaining 5% of Class A interests and all non-managing, non-voting Class B interests. The exact overall economic ownership split is not publicly disclosed. Orca is the single PortCo; Walleye, its holding company, Bay Shore and the individual generating units are subsidiaries or assets beneath the platform. No Orca-specific sale or pending ownership transfer was identified through August 14, 2026.

BUSINESS OVERVIEW

Orca Acquisitions, LLC is an ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VI and Olympus Power joint-venture platform that indirectly owns Walleye Power, LLC through Walleye Energy Holdings, LLC.

Walleye owns and operates the Bay Shore merchant-power and industrial-steam facility in Oregon, Ohio. A June 2026 FERC filing reports 136 MW of summer-rated steam generation and a 16 MW oil-fired unit. ArcLight Orca Holdings, LLC holds 95% of Orca's Class A managing interests, appoints two management-committee members and controls day-to-day decisions. Olympus affiliates hold the remaining 5% of Class A interests and all non-managing, non-voting Class B interests. The exact overall economic ownership split is not publicly disclosed. Orca is the single PortCo; Walleye, its holding company, Bay Shore and the individual generating units are subsidiaries or assets beneath the platform. No Orca-specific sale or pending ownership transfer was identified through August 14, 2026.

api.name: Virginia International Gateway
api.description: Virginia International Gateway is the private owner of the highly automated VIG marine container terminal in Portsmouth, Virginia. The terminal handles containerized cargo for ocean carriers, beneficial cargo owners, railroads, motor carriers and regional supply chains; Astatine describes approximately 2 million TEU of annual throughput capacity. Virginia International Gateway, Inc. owns the terminal, the Virginia Port Authority leases it under a long-term facilities lease, and the authority's Virginia International Terminals subsidiary operates it. The facility opened in 2007 as APM Terminals Virginia. Affiliates of Alinda-managed funds and USS acquired it in August 2014 and renamed it VIG. Astatine now lists one VIG profile as Active and a separate Fund II investment as exited in 2019. The Virginia Port Authority's August 2025 final official statement identifies USS and PSP as the current underlying owners, supporting an active Astatine manager attribution and an active PSP direct-owner association while preserving the realized Fund II period. The active Astatine fund or managed-account vehicle, manager-level stake and entry date, plus PSP's entry date and percentage, are not publicly disclosed. No later full sale, signed pending exit or transfer of terminal title to the port authority was identified through August 18, 2026. APM Terminals Virginia is the predecessor name; VPA, VIT, lease interests, bonds, cranes and expansion projects are not separate PortCos.
